name: Question 14
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14010574/assets/8f9b82ba9e1ed640aedd6f67118beef2d88c419bbd046171cca5b527c2b407a5.png)

Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of 
${\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [-4,-2]$, the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-2,2),$ and the line segment for $x\in (2,4].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,2).$ The corresponding region is a combination of an inverted semi-circle of radius $2$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh-\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =4(3)-\frac{1}{2}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =12-2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (2,4].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =6+12-2\pi +3 \\  & =21-2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Given the graph of y=f(x) above, find the value of ∫−44f(x)dx.

a
12+2π
b
21−2π
c
14+2π
d
18−4π
e
19−2π
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The graph consists of 3 parts: the line segment for x∈[−4,−2], the arc of the semi-circle for x∈[−2,2), and the line segment for x∈(2,4]. So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get ∫−44f(x)dx=∫−4−2f(x)dx⏟A1+∫−22f(x)dx⏟A2+∫24f(x)dx⏟A3.

  • The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−4,−2]. The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula A1=bh=2⋅3=6.

  • The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈[−2,2). The corresponding region is a combination of an inverted semi-circle of radius 2 and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula A2=bh−12πr2=4(3)−12π(2)2=12−2π.

  • The 3rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the x-axis, where x∈(2,4]. The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula A3=12⋅bh=12⋅2⋅3=3.

Finally, we obtain ∫−44f(x)dx=A1+A2+A3=6+12−2π+3=21−2π.
